title: Answer engines
purpose: When a customer says an AI assistant told them something wrong about us, or buyers ask assistants what to buy, open Answer engines to see what they say, fix it at the source and check it stuck.
fires: the founder typing our name into ChatGPT on a phone now and then, the AI-visibility vendor's share-of-voice deck, and the habit of hoping the assistants get it right.
not_for: a store whose buyers do not research before buying, like cheap impulse items, or one whose normal search basics are not yet in order.

jobs.job: When a customer says 'ChatGPT told me your product does X' and it does not, help me find what the assistants say about us, where they learned it and fix it at the source, so I stop selling a promise we cannot keep
jobs.circumstance: A support ticket or a return note quotes an AI assistant, the claim is wrong, the founder has no idea how many other buyers heard the same thing

progress.functional: know what each assistant says about the product, which facts are wrong, and which page or site they came from
progress.emotional: stop the helpless feeling that a machine is making promises in my name
progress.social: answer the customer and the team with a clear fix, and look like a brand that tells the truth

jobs.hire_today: nothing that works, so the founder types a few questions into ChatGPT on a phone, shrugs and replies to the one customer
jobs.fire: the phone check and the one-off apology

forces.push: a wrong promise turns into returns, angry tickets and bad reviews
forces.pull: the wrong facts found, traced to a source and fixed
forces.habit: we cannot control what the assistants say, so we do not try
forces.anxiety: what if we fix our site and the assistant keeps saying it anyway

jobs.little_hire: every time a ticket or review quotes an assistant, and once a month

watch.metric: wrong facts about us in assistant answers on the fixed prompt set, by assistant, monthly
watch.source: brand brain prompt-run log (a fixed set of buyer questions asked of each assistant; no platform reports this)

drives.metric: tickets and returns that cite an assistant's claim, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 assistants say the socks are machine-dryable on high, they are not. After: the care page and 2 old reviews fixed, 2 of 3 assistants correct within 6 weeks.
jobs.not_for: a store whose buyers never research before buying

jobs.circumstance: Month end, returns up, a few notes say 'the AI said it runs large'

progress.emotional: stop the vague worry and know the size of the problem
progress.social: show the team and partners that AI answers are a real cost, with numbers

jobs.hire_today: nothing, because no one tags tickets or returns by where the wrong idea came from
jobs.fire: the untagged ticket and the shrug

forces.push: wrong answers cost money in ways no one counts
forces.pull: the cost per wrong fact, so the worst gets fixed first
forces.habit: tickets are tagged by product, not by cause
forces.anxiety: what if customers blame the AI to get an easy return

watch.metric: tickets and returns tagged 'assistant said', by fact, 30 day
watch.source: Gorgias tags and Shopify return reasons

drives.metric: refund and support cost tied to assistant claims, 90 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 tickets tagged. After: 38 in a month, 25 about sizing, costing $1,900 in returns.
jobs.not_for: a store that gets no tickets mentioning AI assistants
